notes.title: Women's World Cup
notes.content:
[h2]Women's World Cup[/h2]

The new women's tournament closely follows the 2027 format for qualifiers, with some adjustments due to simulator limitations. 

- UEFA qualifiers use a league system with promotion and relegation, and if the host is European, they still participate despite automatic qualification. 

- The UEFA playoff brackets do not strictly adhere to the League A vs League C or League A/B vs League B structure. 

- CONMEBOL qualifiers use a double round robin instead of a single round robin format. 

- AFC and CAF qualifiers have multiple group hosts rather than just one. 

By default, Brazil hosts the 2027 tournament and the USA hosts in 2030. Note that not every official national team is eligible for World Cup qualifiers, with some CONCACAF, CAF, and AFC teams excluded as in the actual competition.

Also, be very careful when adding custom hosts in the editor. Always make sure you select female teams marked with the gender symbol so that you do not accidentally choose a male team. 

[h2]Women's Intercontinental Cup[/h2]

The Women's Intercontinental Cup and 16-team World Cup have been moved to the "Extra" section to make way for the new Women's World Cup.

https://simcups.com

notes.title: Expanded Overseas Territory Cup

The Anglo-French Territory Cup has been renamed the Overseas Territory Cup and expanded to feature four main groups representing overseas territories: French, UK, Americas/OFC (USA, Australia, New Zealand, Chile), and UEFA overseas territories (Netherlands, Spain, Portugal, Denmark). This expansion brings the total number of participating overseas territory teams to 44. Each country’s territories hold their own qualifiers and group stages, with the top two teams from each group advancing to the quarterfinals to compete for the championship.

notes.title: Women's Intercontinental Cup
notes.content:
The Women Intercontinental Cup is inspired by the Leagues Cup 2025 (MLS vs Liga MX). It includes the top 18 UEFA women's national teams grouped together, while the top 18 non-European teams form a separate group. Each team will compete in six matches exclusively against teams from the opposite group, so they never play against their own group mates in the league phase.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/5a068e72d088d8da158ec30e0b3f23fb5432ec2d.png[/img]

Multiple teams may share the same venue. Most women's teams are expected to share the largest stadiums in their countries

notes.title: Head-to-head Tiebreaker Rules
notes.content:
The Gulf Cup has introduced an experimental head-to-head tiebreaker system for the group stage used by the FIFA Club World Cup. When two or more teams are tied on points, their rankings are determined by their head-to-head results.

1. Total points earned in h2h matches.
2. Goal difference in h2h matches.
3. Number of goals scored in h2h matches.

If there are teams that remain tied after applying these criteria, the same criteria are reapplied only to the matches between those level teams. If still unresolved, overall goal difference, goals scored, and then Elo Ratings are used to break the tie.

For example, in the group results below:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/3ffc66626f26a1e490941b24d90d4d641ea64cda.png[/img]

Bahrain and Oman are tied on points. Although Bahrain’s overall goal difference (-2) is worse than Oman’s (+2), Bahrain ranks higher because they won the head-to-head match 1-0. This head-to-head result is what breaks the tie.

notes.title: Import Team Ratings from Any Date between the 1870s and 2025!

The team databases have been revamped with a new section called “[url=https://simcups.com/team-ratings/2025-01-26]Historical team ratings[/url].” A significant change is that you can now import team data from any date between the 1870s and 2025, unlike the previous version with limited period options.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/bb2bb7e767ae193bbd305139d9fc46831360aa89.png[/img]

While the historical elo ratings are based on eloratings.net, some attributes like attack, defense, and mentality are calculated programmatically based on their match results from the selected period.

Other attributes, such as penalty, host advantage, luck, and reputation, rely on data from 2026. However, it’s possible that the penalty attribute will eventually be adjusted based on historical results as more data becomes available.

One important note: non-affiliated and defunct teams will only appear when you import them from the [url=https://simcups.com/downloadable-teams?page=1]downloadable[/url] section, although there are plans to improve this and make them appear automatically in the future.

[h2]Futsal and Women Nations Teams.[/h2]

Due to the groundbreaking nature of today’s updates, the databases for women’s national teams and futsal national teams will be temporarily suspended. The Futsal World Cup competition will also go offline. However, there are also plans to provide you with the option to download these databases and import them directly in the future.

notes.title: New Settings in Editor
notes.content:
The competition format editor has been reorganized into two primary sections for each stage: [b]Basic[/b] and [b]Qualifications[/b]. Depending on the stage type, the [b]Qualifications[/b] section may have two or three sub-sections: [b]Auto-qualified teams[/b], [b]Other stages[/b], and [b]Knockout brackets.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/c135e0bee984796ffff4ca73b27c48a0e7733fb8.png[/img]

In the [b]Other stages[/b] section, you now have the flexibility to select any stages from [b]any competitions[/b], allowing for greater customization of rules. Additionally, if a team is eligible for multiple rules, the simulator automatically selects the next highest-ranked team to fill available spots.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/6bb063b233505b0132b70384e0cec14adb3784f6.png[/img]

For example, in the Confederations group stage, the qualifications include World Cup champions, runners-up, and other major continental tournament champions. If Spain were to win both the EURO and World Cup, the simulator would automatically select the EURO Cup runner-up to fill the available spot.

[h2]Simulation all until[/h2]

This setting enables you to specify when the simulator should stop further match simulation. You have three options to choose from:

- “Stop when the current stage is completed”: This option tells the simulator to stop the simulation when all matches of the current stage are finished.

- “Stop when all stages under a specific phase / tab are completed”: This option is useful for World Cup qualifiers, where you want to simulate all matches across all continental qualifiers.

- “Stop until the current round is completed”: This option is used for knockout stages.

These settings are typically not required for editing, but they are provided for those who wish to experiment with various scenarios.

notes.title: Humble World Cup Updated Format
notes.content:
Humble World Cup Updated Format

The tournament format has been updated to become more similar to the format of the AFC Cup.

A total of 56 of the lowest-ranked teams will participate in the World Cup, with CONIFA teams now eligible for the event. The tournament will be hosted in a neutral country ranked between 1 and 20 so the host will never participate in the event.

[h3]Tournament Structure:[/h3]

[h3]1st round[/h3]

A preliminary knockout stage for the 16 lowest-ranked teams. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/85cf03e93413c982c880206eb8c298fddd45ef35.png[/img]

[h3]2nd round[/h3]

The winners from the 1st round will join 40 additional teams, forming a total of 48 teams divided into 12 groups. All group winners will qualify for the finals. Teams ranked 13th to 32nd will advance to the 4th round, while teams ranked 33rd to 48th will enter the 3rd round.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/f091f24034a9af13a5a6bd31eb8ef999e7f42050.png[/img]

[h3]3rd round[/h3]

This round will consist of a playoff knockout stage for 15 teams, with one team receiving a bye. The four playoff winners will qualify for the 4th round.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/4d9fcb82468178070048d1308f85f18e7c22cebf.png[/img]

[h3]4th Round[/h3]

This is a group stage with 4 teams per group. The top 12 teams will qualify for the finals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/c5f5be2d74b005d6fa14ba26029f81cd3634dc76.png[/img]

[h3]Finals[/h3]

The finals feature a 24-team and a knockout stage like the EURO Cup.

notes.title: Historical Match Trends
notes.content:
A trend is an experimental feature that may affect match styles across different periods. Currently, there are four default trends spanning from 1870 to 2034 (From Aggressive to Defensive):

[b]Pre-1960[/b]: 
Aggressive - This trend reflects the early days of the sport when teams embraced an attack-minded approach. You can find there are a lot of high-scoring matches during this era.

[b]1960s to 1998[/b]: 
Normal - The influence of total football and Italian's Catenaccio style ended the Aggressive approach.

[b]2002 to 2018[/b]: 
Defensive - Particularly following Greece's EURO victory, which emphasized a strategy of strong defense.

[b]2022 to 2034[/b]: 
Normal - Reinstating a balanced approach similar to earlier trends.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/728da6e7e1c8fa51c31f4088636761f520561cb3.png[/img]

Whenever the simulator is unable to find an existing trend, it will automatically create a new one, with the "Normal" approach being the most commonly generated style.

While this feature may increase the likelihood of certain outcomes, both teams' elo ratings and other attributes remain the key factor in how a match result unfolds.

[h2]Match Styles and Intensity[/h2]

The match style and intensity are two new concepts that set the stage for how matches are simulated.

The [b]match style[/b] influences the number of scoring opportunities the teams tend to receive. It has three styles:

[list]
[*] Aggressive: More chances; Least common.
[*] Conservative: Fewer chances; Lesser common.
[*] Normal: Balanced number of chances; Most common.
[/list]

However, teams' abilities remain the key factor in determining results.

The [b]match intensity[/b] indicates the likelihood of teams getting incidents. Matches between rivals, matches involving defending champions or matches with higher prestige, are more prone to incidents.

notes.title: Road to 270 Mini Game
notes.content:
The new "[url=https://simcups.com/general-election/2026]Road to 270[/url]" section is inspired by the U.S. electoral system, featuring 51 match-ups, each representing a U.S. state and its corresponding electoral votes. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/ba80db71288b4fe8494a63de02a2ab858b991a06.png[/img]

At the beginning, the simulator randomly selects 102 teams and divides them into two camps: red and blue. Each match-up pits one blue team (always positioned on the left) against one blue team (positioned on the right). The winner of each match-up secures the electoral votes for their camp. The first camp to reach 270 votes will be declared the election winner.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/865663b7df7bded716d3cc3fcfe7d8f06a6dca19.png[/img]

[h2]Key Features[/h2]

1. Match-ups involving states with higher electoral votes, such as California and Texas, will always feature the strongest teams from each camp, while those with fewer electoral votes will involve weaker teams. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/b75ed3248df26078cfa1a8685b2903ad23df7cd2.png[/img]

2. All match-ups are randomly ordered, adding an element of unpredictability and excitement to the gameplay.

3. Winners of each match-up will have their Elo ratings updated, reflecting their performance in these simulated contests. Elo ratings are a method for calculating relative skill levels based on match outcomes.

4. Purge Votes Button: A "Purge votes" button allows players to reset all match-ups.

5. You can click the "Simulate all" button to run all match-ups simultaneously.

notes.title: 16-team World Cup
notes.content:
The [url=https://simcups.com]Forever World Cup Simulator[/url] has just introduced a vintage 16-team World Cup tournament, which borrows some elements from the 1974 World Cup held in West Germany. 

[h2]Qualification Process[/h2]

[h3]CAF (Africa): 1 slot[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/bb682cfaab04d2c76615424148384cf9491e257b.png[/img]

[h3]AFC + OFC (Asia and Oceania): 1 slot[/h3]

The lowest-ranked 28 teams will compete in a preliminary round. The best 7 teams will join other 29 teams to compete in a Swiss model group stage, where the top eight qualify for a knockout stage to determine one finalist.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/1a2e336605169dbf6e3450825a134a976f77c7ab.png[/img]

[h3]CONCACAF (North America): 1 slot[/h3]

All 41 CONCACAF teams will enter a preliminary stage, with the top 8 progressing to the second round. The best 4 from this round will compete to determine one finalist.

[h3]UEFA (Europe): 8 slots[/h3]

UEFA teams will be split into 9 groups. The top 8 group winners qualify for the finals, while the last group winner faces a South American team in an intercontinental playoff.

Host Nation: 1 slot
The host nation automatically qualifies for the tournament.

[h2]World Cup Finals[/h2]

The finals will feature 16 teams competing in a group stage.

Teams will be divided into 4 groups, with group winners and runners-up advancing to a second group stage. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/bf17379d4c6390b18c24bc66492b95bc36befedd.png[/img]

notes.title: Romance of Three Kingdoms Football League Simulation
notes.content:
Yesterday's update introduced a new tournament: the[url=https://simcups.com] League of Three Kingdoms[/url]! This fantasy league should give you an idea about how to use the editors to create a tournament that is more than football. The league now features [url=https://simcups.com/new-teams?tagId=5]30 factions[/url], including the legendary Wei, Wu, Shu, Yuans, Sima, and other warlords, as they compete fiercely on the football pitch.

[i]League A's factions[/i]:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/1544465d5b2bb6e81d3db70ee1737b69e28fbbac.png[/img]

[i]League B's factions[/i]:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/57f94da8947f0d482115cc8f941b815b55315144.png[/img]

Each team's attributes and ELO ratings are authentically based on their historical significance and power during this era. The Wei faction emerges as a dominant force with an impressive ELO rating of around 2200, while Wu and Shu closely follow at approximately 1900.

The league structure is pretty straightforward: 30 teams are divided into two divisions of 15. The top 2 teams from League B will rise to League A, while the bottom 2 teams in League A will face relegation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/8cb1009623f9dd2b7c1574daac4affe92f1f806d.png[/img]

Rivalries among several factions will enhance the league's dynamics, potentially leading to upsets and unexpected performances from some underdog teams in the simulation.

As the league exists in a fictional universe, it will not interact with real-world football teams, making it best suited for standalone play. Enjoy the unique experience of the League of Three Kingdoms!

notes.title: 24-team World Cup Simulation
notes.content:
The vintage [url=https://simcups.com]24-Team World Cup[/url] has been released! Its qualification process is similar to the 1994 tournament format.

[h2]Qualified Teams by Confederation[/h2]

[list]
[*] UEFA: 12 slots
[*] AFC: 2.25 slots
[*] CAF: 3 slots
[*] CONMEBOL: 4.25 slots
[*] OFC: 0.25 slots
[*] CONCACAF: 1.25 slots
[*] Host Nation: 1 slot
[/list]

[h2]Qualification Process Overview[/h2]

[b]UEFA[/b]: In the 1st round, the lowest-ranked 20 teams will compete in a round-robin stage, divided into 5 groups. The top team from each group will advance to the 2nd round, where 39 teams will fight for 12 slots in the World Cup finals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/a6411d2edb72469c7304ffb23853d5083d95830a.png[/img]

[b]CONMEBOL[/b]: The South American teams will be divided into two groups, the top 4 team will advance for the final, and the best third placed team will advance for the inter-continental playoff.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/6de04f4108b21a91ed53b5c53202fb2737b40acc.png[/img]

[b]AFC[/b]: The top six teams in the 2nd round will enter the 3rd round, which features a single-group round-robin format. In this stage, the top 2 teams will secure their spots in the World Cup finals, while the third-place team will qualify for the inter-playoff.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/ae93c3e7d63ddad47c036768c39d74b65545d0f5.png[/img]

[b]OFC[/b]: The second round will consist of 2 groups of 8 teams. The winner of each group will enter a knockout round to determine the slot for the inter-continental playoff.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/10740d8152924a47fc1acb55fadb97116a800966.png[/img]

[b]CONCACAF[/b]: The top 4 teams in the 2nd round will enter a single group round robin stage to decide the single slot for the World Cup finals. The second placed team will enter the inter-playoff.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/b5a41525b54ceec505144ba2e6b64cacb50c9b96.png[/img]

The inter-continental playoff will have 4 teams from AFC, CONMEBOL, OFC and CONCACAF to fight for the last slot in the World Cup finals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/7c7890bdf6a88e4a76e99e7f4fcac0d0eb18428f.png[/img]

[h2]Customizable Starting Year[/h2]

You can change the default starting year of 2026 to any World Cup year. Whether it is 1600 or 2024, the simulator should be capable to handle these adjustments seamlessly, but keep in mind that the year cannot be changed once events have started.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/e7f212d0b46820f588f4bf36eaa6073f221e5662.png[/img]

Changing the starting year will also update the historical identities of certain teams. For instance, if the starting year is set before 2006, Serbia will be replaced by Yugoslavia, complete with the Yugoslavia flag. Currently, there are a dozen teams with historical identities available, including China, India, Canada, Spain, and various African nations, but rest assured that more identities will be added regularly.

[i]Some teams' flags has changed when you set the starting year to 1952.[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/d34833670d623f5599e7a32f6e2bab0a02cb00e5.png[/img]

Like many things in the simulator, the team identities are customizable in the "identity" tab of the [url=https://simcups.com/update-team/9]team editors[/url]. You can add, remove or update the corresponding names, flags, squad images and victory images.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/5bcadc49ae821443965e2dea3774be305e2c98e4.png[/img]

However, changing the year does not automatically change the attributes and elo ratings of all teams. You must import a [url=https://simcups.com/team-databases]related database[/url] (if available) corresponding to that year.

[h2]Competition editor[/h2]

[h3] Auto or manual team selection[/h3]
A "Team selection" setting has been added to each stage in the [url=https://simcups.com/competition-editor/1]editor[/url]. notes.title: Steam Cloud Support
notes.content:
The Forever World Cup Simulator now supports Steam's Cloud Sync feature! This allows you to seamlessly access your simulation data across multiple devices, cross-platform.
How to Use Steam Cloud Sync:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/c2db28318eb51fb3c932cf0a1e61d0bd646df463.png[/img]

When you click the "Export" button on the homepage, save your files in the following directory path based on your operating system:

Windows users:
[b]%USERPROFILE%/My Documents/forever-world-cup-simulator/steam-cloud/

[/b]Linux and macOS users:
[b]~/Documents/forever-world-cup-simulator/steam-cloud/
[/b]

Once you've saved your files in this directory, Steam will automatically upload them to the Steam Cloud when you launch or exit the Steam app.

The feature works with both the web and Steam versions. So if you export saves in the web version, as long as you store it in the above directory path, the Steam app will take care of it.

Please note that the game will not automatically import your sync data on start. You still need to click "Import" to select the sync files from the document folder.

Storage Limits per User:

Maximum storage: 5GB
Maximum number of files: 1,000

Start using Steam Cloud Sync today to keep your Forever World Cup Simulator data safe and accessible across all your devices!

notes.title: New Sections in Competition Editor.
notes.content:
The competition editor has just added two new sections to make the process of selecting qualifying teams more flexible and intuitive. 

[b]Qualifications[/b]

The new "Qualification" section replaces the previous playoff, qualified, relegated, and promoted slots. This section allows users to create custom qualification rules with or without host conditions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/42bbd1bc51edbf0c1088fcb43b66e1c0e15f0575.png[/img]

The editable fields include:

[list]
[*]Stages where the qualified teams come from. —whether group or knockout—along with optional host conditions.
[*]Specify minimum and maximum overall standings to determine which teams qualify. For instance, if you want to select teams that lost in the quarter-finals, you can set the minimum overall standing to "5" and the maximum to "8."
[*]The highlight colors for qualified teams in group standings if the source stage is a group stage. 
[/list]

Feel free to create as many rules as necessary to accommodate various hosting conditions. The simulator will intelligently identify and apply the relevant rules for selecting qualified teams.

[b]Host conditions[/b]

The section sets the criteria for how the simulator selects hosts for a competition.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45111527/dc2cf57294c8eeb22fb9b2825eef2c2134be5d6d.png[/img]

The editable fields include:
 
[list]
[*]Number of hosts that can be selected
[*]Confederations of the hosts
[*]How often specific host conditions should be applied.
[/list]


However, there is a limitation with this new host condition concept. Selecting multi-hosts that are outside the default host conditions will not work. For example, if you try to select a European host and an Asian host for the World Cup, it will not work because there are no built-in host conditions for that combination.
To make this kind of multi-host scenario possible, you would need to create a new custom host condition and add corresponding stage adjustments (like team count, group count, etc.) and qualification rules. 
Unfortunately, this process is very time-consuming and requires a lot of trial and error to get right.
